A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AudioX. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained methods, experiments, and figures can be matched despite substantial scientific revisions and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original audio/music generation experiments, inpainting and completion results, masking ablations, and a human evaluation in Section 5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v3 reports original generation experiments, new instruction-following evaluations and data/fusion ablations, alongside retained empirical results in Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: v2's input-masking and direct-concatenation design is replaced by Multimodal Adaptive Fusion, using gates, learnable queries, attention, and residual updates. v3 also adds Synchformer synchronization features. The captioning pipeline changes from Qwen2-Audio annotation to Gemini annotation followed by Qwen2-Audio augmentation.

E1.justification: v3 adds AudioTime training/evaluation and T2A-bench evaluation, extending coverage to explicit event counts, ordering, duration, and timestamps. IF-caps supplies structured instruction supervision over the existing audio/music sources. Inpainting, music completion, and image-to-audio coverage remain in the appendix.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds VATT and VAB specifically to VGGSound video-to-audio comparisons. The new instruction-following comparisons include Make-An-Audio2, and Table 3 evaluates AudioSetCaps as an external caption-source baseline. Comparator sets in the other retained experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported batch size changes from 96 to 48 and training time from approximately 3.2k to 4k GPU hours; Table A.1 revises training composition and sample counts. New protocols include T2A-bench's four groups of 500 prompts and two-stage Gemini judging, plus AudioTime temporal metrics.

E4.justification: v2's mask-ratio sweep and no/feature/input-masking comparison disappear. v3 adds caption-source and augmentation comparisons in Table 3 and MAF, gate, and query ablations in Table 4. The unified-versus-specialist and modality-combination analyses are retained, moving from Figure 6 to Figure A.3.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and average human ratings without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The user-study plot is retained unchanged as v3 Figure A.2.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises AudioX results: AudioCaps T2A IS/FAD changes from 12.09/1.86 to 12.48/1.59, while VGGSound T2A IS changes from 20.27 to 19.58. These accompany changed architecture and training, rather than isolating a same-setting improvement. v3 adds instruction-following and curation/MAF results and removes masking results. Inpainting, completion, image-generation, and user-study outcomes are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 introduces mathematical correctness rules for the new benchmark accuracies: detecting all required categories, exact counts/order, and timestamps within a one-second tolerance. The diffusion equations (2)–(4) remain unchanged, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace masking-centered contributions and the two original caption datasets with MAF, IF-caps, and structured data curation. Superior fine-grained instruction following and cross-modal regularization become headline claims. The overarching unified audio/music generation claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 explains benefits through masking-induced robustness, reduced information leakage, and video redundancy. v3 instead attributes improvements to suppressing cross-modal interference and textual supervision regularizing other modalities. Sections 5.3–5.5 additionally distinguish fidelity from instruction following and interpret performance through interaction between data curation and fusion.

D1.justification: v3 adds annotation schemas, augmentation examples, benchmark composition, and automated-judging specifications in Appendices A.1–A.3. It documents MAF's 60M parameters and Synchformer's 25-fps features. Appendix A.4.1 newly specifies 3,000 stylized VGGSound keyframes for the retained image experiment. Benchmark/evaluator release is newly promised; code and dataset availability still uses future tense.

R1.justification: The masking-focused related-work discussion is removed, while dataset and temporal-control positioning expands through works including AudioSetCaps, AudioTime, and Make-An-Audio2. The novelty argument shifts toward fine-grained supervision and controllability. Publication updates for retained works such as MMAudio and VidMuse do not constitute new research additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method narrative, ablation discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related work is reorganized, Section 5.5 adds a discussion, and several task evaluations and modality analyses move into a reorganized appendix with extensive annotation and evaluation explanations.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a single-column conference layout, redraws the annotation and model diagrams, and replaces the capability panel with instruction-following charts. It adds word clouds, benchmark-distribution graphics, and new comparison/ablation tables. Retained task tables and user-study/modality plots move to the appendix, while the masking plot disappears.

improvement.justification: v2 supported its caption-data contribution mainly through general benchmark performance. v3 adds direct caption-source comparisons, fusion-component ablations, and explicit instruction-following evaluations on two benchmarks (Tables 2–4), substantially strengthening evidence for its contributions. Appendix schemas and scoring rules also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including unreconciled IF-caps clip-versus-caption totals and Appendix A.3's judge example discussing a wave crash despite a catapult prompt.
